caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.174 of 2018
lawyer:
Mr. Ali Imam Khaled Rahim, Advocate instructed by Mr. Md. Bodrul Islam, Advocate-on-Record   For the Petitioner

For the Respondents None represented
parties:
Md. Jamal Uddin ------ Petitioner
-Vs-
Md. Afaz Uddin and others ------- Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The facts, relevant for disposal of this petition, are that the plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.193 of 2007 in the Court of the Assistant Judge, 5th Court, Gazipur for cancellation of a deed. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that there is 1.87 acres land including 5 decimals land of the suit property in CS Khatian No.4, CS Plot Nos.13, 14, 15, 20 described in schedule-'Ka'. Md. Abbas Ali got 5.25 decimals land by inheritance and during possession and enjoyment, he transferred the suit property to his younger brother, Md. Sarbesh Ali through Hiba-bil-ewaz Deed No.10426 dated 17.06.1998. The plaintiffs got 5.25 decimals land from Md. Sarbesh Ali of Mouza-Uttar Krishnapur by registered deed of gift bearing No. 13389 dated 26.07.1998. On the other hand, plaintiff No.1 got 7 decimals land from his mother. Talemonnessa, in SA Khatian No.85 and SA Plot No.326 by Hiba-bil-ewaz deed No.19350 dated 07.10.2002 described in schedule`Kha' to the plaint. The plaintiffs got title and possession of the said property and have been enjoying the property by constructing house, growing various kinds of trees thereon and the suit land was mutated in the names of the plaintiffs and they have been residing thereon with family. 

 4. Defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the material allegations as to engaging him as attorney made in the plaint admitting the chain of title of the plaintiffs in the suit property contending, inter alia, that the plaintiffs, husband and wife, voluntarily on their proposal and acceptance by defendant No.1 sold out the property at a consideration of taka 24,000.00 by the registered deed; that after his purchase, he has been possessing the land peacefully and paid rent, development tax after mutating his name in the concerned khatian. 

 10. Mr. Ali Imam Khaled Rahim, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that the Courts below have concurrently found that the deed of the instant suit is a registered deed and the plaintiffs have failed to prove the allegation of fraud as described in the plaint by adducing any documentary as well as oral evidence, but the High Court Division without controverting the concurrent findings reversed the judgment and decree of the Courts below. He further submits that the appellate Court below being the final Court of facts has correctly found that PW1 herself did not support the plaint in her deposition and other PWs did not dis-close nothing about the allegation of fraud in execution of the deed of the suit and the High Court Division without controverting the said findings of the last Court of facts erred in law in decreeing the suit reversing the judgment and decree of the Courts below. He further submits that the plaintiffs completely failed to prove their positive case that the plaintiffs appeared before the Sub-registry Office to execute a power of attorney in favour of defendant No.1 to conduct two Miscellaneous Case Nos.34 of 1996-1997 and 35 of 1996-1997 before the concerned Assistant Commissioner (Land) by producing any document including any document of the said Miscellaneous Cases which were claimed to be disposed of and, therefore, the High Court Division erred in law in decreeing the suit reversing the judgment and decree of the Courts below. He further submits that though 4 plots are mentioned in the deed of the gift of the plaintiffs, but actually they have got possession from only Plot No. 15 out of 4 plots and in the same way, the plaintiffs have sold 5 decimals land from two khatians which were adjacent to each other and amicably handed over possession from schedule 'Kha' to the suit to defendant No.1 and he mutated his name in the said khatian, but the High Court Division reversed the concurrent findings of the Courts below in holding that there is no definite assertion as to the transferable quantum of the land from each schedule which is misconception and liable to be set aside. He further submits that there are two schedules of the suit, first one in Krishnapur mouza another one in Bagia mouza and the plaintiffs amicably handed over possession of 5 decimals land from Bagia mouza to defendant No.1 out of two mouzas as they were in possession of only Plot No.15 out of 4 plots as admitted in paragraph No.5 of the plaint and PW2 did not disclose that the plain-tiffs are possessing in Bagia mouza and PW3 was declared hostile and cross-examined by the plaintiffs, but nothing has been disclosed in favour of the plaintiffs specially regarding possession of Bagia mouza inasmuch as the plaintiffs have been possessing the land of Krisnapur mouza (at present-East Kholapara) which is schedule-'Ka' to the suit land and in nature homestead land (t) land and the defendant-petitioner has been possessing the land Mentioned in schedule-`Kha' Bagia Mouza which is in nature chala land (Fgt) as per the last record of right, but the High Court Division without considering properly the deposition of PW2 and PW3 to that effect reversed the decree of the Courts below in holding that PW2 and PW3 deposed asserting the possession of the plaintiffs which is absolutely misreading and misconstruction of the material evidence on record. He further submits that in a suit for cancellation of deed, the High Court Division unlawfully considered the fact of mutation in the khatian which was subsequent to the alleged case of action and in no way related to the alleged fact of fraud, moreover khatian can be corrected in a proper proceeding and therefore, the High Court Division passed the impugned judgment upon meresurmises and conjecture. He further submits that DW3 is the attesting witness of the deed and stated in his deposition that “বাদী বাদীর স্ত্রী বিক্রি করেছে। বিবাদী কিনতে ১৪,০০০/- টাকায় বিক্রি হয়েছে। টাকা পয়সা লেনদেন হয়েছে। বাদী ও তার স্ত্রী আমার সামনে স্বাক্ষর করে।”and the plaintiffs cross-examined him but did not put any suggestion denying the execution of the deed or the plaintiffs did not produce any evidence disproving the payment of consideration and DW2 in his cross-examination corroborated- the fact of giving consideration money to the effect that ‘লেনদেন করতে দেখেছি’ but the High Court Division reversed the decree of the Courts below in holding that the statements of DW3 cannot be the basis in absence of other credible evidence though, on the other hand, in the conclusion of the said findings, the High Court Division correctly held that the deed was executed with consideration which is self-contradictory and absolutely misreading and misconstruction of the material evidence 'on record and therefore, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. 

 14. On the other hand, defendant No.1(present petitioner) denied the aforesaid claim of the plaintiff-respondents and counterclaimed that the plaintiff-respondents are husband and wife who voluntarily proposed to sell out the suit property and defendant No.1(present petitioner) accepted the proposal and consideration of the suit land was fixed at taka 24,000.00 and accordingly, the kabala was registered and since then defendant No.1(present petitioner) has been possessing the land peacefully after mutating his name in the suit khatian. 

 On the point of consideration money, though the Court below, that is the trial Court, relied on the evidence of DW3, the attesting witness, who came before the Court to prove the execution of the purported deed his statement “চব্বিশ হাজার টাকা আদান প্রদান” cannot be the basis in absence of other credible evidence for coming to the conclusion that document has been executed and registered with consideration money. Further, it appears that exhibit- `Kha' series, namely, the mutated Khatian, rent receipt and duplicate carbon receipt on behalf of the defendant have been relied upon by both the Courts below although the same were obtained by the defendant during pendency of the suit. Moreover, definite case of the defendant is that he obtained properties from two schedules though exhibit-`Kha' series relates only the proper-ties of one schedule, i.e. schedule No.2. Since the document itself shows that by practicing fraud and/or mis-representation and/or wrong promise, it naturally became a voidable document and as such I see merit in the Rule."
